title: How many millimetres make a kilometre?
description: A kilometre is changed into metres and then into millimetres by chaining two facts. A last step divides back to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: chain two unit changes by multiplying the two factors. Watch for children who multiply by only one thousand.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q11
video_script.why: The child has changed one unit of length into the next and now chains two changes from kilometres to millimetres.
video_script.substitution: Change kilometres into metres, then metres into millimetres, by multiplying by one thousand each time.
video_script.anchor: one kilometre, one metre and one millimetre drawn as three sizes
video_script.payoff_line: Chain the two facts by multiplying one thousand by one thousand
video_script.fraction_reading: no fractions are read in this video
video_script.design: The three sizes stay in the anchor band. The two facts chain in the working band, the two thousands are multiplied, and a last step divides the answer back down to one kilometre.
open_questions: The book prints ten lakh millimetres; the script keeps that wording and says lakh aloud.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a kilometre, a metre and a millimetre drawn as three sizes; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about millimetres in a kilometre.
<bookmark mark='list'/>A kilometre is a long distance, and a millimetre is very short.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many millimetres make one kilometre?

beats.on_screen: the three sizes stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
1 km = 1000 m and 1 m = 1000 mm drawn as a chain of two links

marks.km: 1 km = 1000 m is drawn as the first link
marks.m: 1 m = 1000 mm is drawn as the second link

narration: <bookmark mark='km'/>A kilometre has one thousand metres, and a metre has one thousand millimetres.
<bookmark mark='m'/>We can chain these two facts together.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 m = 1000 mm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one kilometre equals one thousand metres, and one metre equals one thousand millimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the millimetres in 1 km
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the millimetres in one kilometre.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 km = 1000 m, and each metre = 1000 mm

marks.each: each of the 1000 metres is marked as 1000 mm

narration: <bookmark mark='km'/>Step one, one kilometre is one thousand metres.
<bookmark mark='each'/>Each of those metres is one thousand millimetres.

marks.lakh: the product is written with commas as ten lakh

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, multiply one thousand by one thousand.
One thousand times one thousand is ten lakh.
<bookmark mark='lakh'/>That makes ten lakh millimetres in one kilometre.

marks.chk: the millimetres are divided by one thousand

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step three, put the answer back by dividing ten lakh millimetres by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='back'/>That gives one thousand metres, and dividing again gives one kilometre.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Chain the two facts by multiplying one thousand by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='val'/>One kilometre is ten lakh millimetres.
